claims.text: Replacing EAM references with active-learning deep-learning interatomic potentials will improve reference–target phase-space overlap in multicomponent high-entropy alloys near melting.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
Liquid-state disorder is pronounced near and at the high melting temperatures of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Active learning can be used to generate a deep-learning potential from ab initio calculations for solid and liquid configurations.
The proposed method is applicable to refractory high-entropy alloys containing five or more metallic components.
The applicable temperature range is approximately 2000–3000 K.
Both solid and liquid phases are present in the proposed 2000–3000 K range.
Deep-learning potentials can represent both ordered and disordered configurations encountered in solid and liquid states with high fidelity.
High-fidelity representation of ordered and disordered configurations improves reference–target phase-space overlap.
Training on extensive ab initio datasets spanning diverse solid and liquid atomic arrangements enables a deep-learning potential to capture configurational diversity.
TOR-TILD EAM references cannot adequately represent the full configurational complexity of the ab initio liquid.
The proposed deep-learning reference will qualitatively reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch compared with TOR-TILD EAM references.
EAM-based TOR-TILD free-energy calculations have known limitations caused by inadequate representation of liquid configurations.
The hypothesis should apply near the melting points of high-entropy alloys containing multiple refractory elements.
The method's effectiveness may decrease for compositions or temperatures substantially outside the deep-learning potential's training range.
